title: Grateful Dead Live at Woodstock Music on 1969-08-16
lineage: Panasonic SV-3700 > Cardas cable S/PDIF > Edirol UA-5 > analog out > Korg MR-1 DFF @ [1bit/2.8 mhz] Rate Conversion: AudioGate to [24bit/96 khz] Mastering: In WaveLab with L3 Waves Multimaximizer > TLH > Flac

ai_review.summary: Fair soundboard capture of the Woodstock set with Pigpen’s marathon “Turn On Your Lovelight” standing out.
ai_review.review: The recording is an average‑quality soundboard tape that benefits from a bit of EQ work, but it is listenable.  The show itself isn’t hailed as a classic; reviewers note it was “not the worst,” with the 45‑minute Pigpen‑led rendition of “Turn On Your Lovelight” being the only specific highlight.  Overall sentiment is mixed, leaning mildly positive.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviews are few and vague; show quality appears average with one notable jam, while recording quality is decent but not exceptional.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear enough for a soundboard source but listeners are advised to use EQ; no specific drop‑outs or distortion mentioned.

show_quality.setlist_flow: No detailed commentary on set structure; the only highlighted moment is Pigpen’s extended jam, suggesting a fairly average overall flow.

band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen leads a 45‑minute “Turn On Your Lovelight,” noted as a highlight and evidence he wasn’t on LSD that day.
